title: 2006 AMC 10A Problem 23
statement: Circles with centers \(A\) and \(B\) have radii \(3\) and \(8,\) respectively. A common internal tangent touches the circles at \(C\) and \(D,\) as shown. Lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersect at \(E,\) and \(AE = 5.\) What is \(CD?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(AC \perp CD,\) we have \(CE = \sqrt{AE^2 - AC^2}\) \(= \sqrt{25 - 9}\) \(= 4.\)

Because \(\triangle ACE \sim \triangle BDE,\) \(\frac{DE}{CE} = \frac{BD}{AC},\) so \(DE = 4 \cdot \frac{8}{3} = \frac{32}{3}.\)

Then \(CD = CE + DE\) \(= 4 + \frac{32}{3}\) \(= \frac{44}{3}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Radii \(AC\) and \(BD\) are perpendicular to the tangent \(CD\)
